issues.problem: These negatives are framed as testing the 'fire-emoji reaction' condition, but Kenji and Robert are already excluded on the prior condition (they did not author the #engineering circuit-tracer OOM message at all — Kenji's message lacks the OOM keyword content match in the intended sense and Robert's is a reply, not the identified message). The mechanical auxiliary path (channel_members.user_id = messages.user_id, filtered to the OOM message in #engineering) alone already uniquely resolves to Lukas without ever consulting the reaction condition, so these negatives do not actually exercise the reaction-based exclusion they claim to demonstrate.
issues.repair: Either drop the 'reaction condition' framing from these negative roles' reasons (describe them simply as same-channel members who are not the message author), or restructure the auxiliary query so a same-channel, correctly-authored-but-wrong-reaction case would genuinely need the reaction filter to be excluded (e.g., have a second person post an equally-qualifying OOM-circuit-tracer message in #engineering with a non-fire reaction, so the reaction condition does real discriminating work).

issues.problem: The task instructs the solver to 'confirm that author has also left a fire-emoji reaction somewhere,' which has no bounded search procedure via documented APIs (no search-by-reaction or search-by-user endpoint exists); confirming this requires exhaustively walking every conversation the actor belongs to and checking reactions.get per message. Because the underlying answer does not actually depend on locating this reaction (per the mechanical construction noted above), this adds substantial solver burden without functioning as a genuine correctness-determining condition in this instance.
issues.repair: Either remove the open-ended 'somewhere' reaction confirmation requirement from the prompt/task text (since it is not doing real filtering work here), or restructure the case so at least one plausible negative author would only be excluded by actually checking the reaction, making the search meaningful.

rationale: The compiled selector correctly and uniquely resolves to the (C03IJKL9012, U_LUKAS) membership: the auxiliary path binds channel_members.user_id to the author of the unique #engineering message containing both 'circuit-tracer' and 'OOM' (message 1706110000.000100), and the focal path's existence check over the fire reaction is satisfied by the seeded U_LUKAS/fire reaction row; checks.computed_matches confirms a single match with a full near-miss population of other #engineering members. The message-location scoping (#engineering) is consistently enforced on both focal and auxiliary paths, correctly excluding the pre-existing DM message from Sophie that also mentions circuit-tracer and OOM. Access is realistic: the actor is a member of #engineering, #model-research, and #core-infra, so all referenced messages/reactions are reachable via documented conversations.history/reactions.get, and conversations.kick is a supported, correctly-scoped state-changing operation with no written_attributes needed. The design therefore passes validity. Quality is only adequate because several of the negative roles built around the 'fire-emoji reaction' condition are redundant with the (sufficient-on-its-own) message-authorship condition, so they do not actually exercise the reaction dimension they are described as testing, and the task's instruction to 'confirm' the reaction 'somewhere' imposes an open-ended, effectively unbounded search that is not load-bearing for correctness in this seed.
